title: Katha Upanishad

content.sanskrit: ॐ उशन्ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ । तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस
content.text:
Now verily, with zeal did Vajasravasa give his whole
possession [as a religious gift]. He had a son, Naciketas by
name.

content.sanskrit: त ह कुमार सन्तं दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धाविवेश सोऽमन्यत
content.text:
Into him, boy as he was, while the sacrificial gifts were
being led up, faith ( sraddha ) entered. He thought to himself:

content.sanskrit:
पीतोदका जग्धतृणा दुग्धदोहा निरिन्द्रियाः ।
अनन्दा नाम ते लोकास्तान्स गच्छति ता ददत्
content.text:
‘ Their water drunk, their grass eaten,
Their milk milked, barren ! —
Joyless ( a-nanda ) certainly are those worlds
He goes to, who gives such [cows] ! ’

content.sanskrit:
स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति ।
द्वितीयं तृतीयं त होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति
content.text:
Then he said to his father : ‘ Papa, to whom will you give
me ? ’ — a second time — a third time.
To him then he said : ‘To Death I give you ! ’

content.sanskrit:
बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः ।
कि स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाऽद्य करिष्यति
content.text:
[Naciketas reflects :]
Of many I go as the first.
Of many I go as an intermediate.
What, pray, has Yama (Death) to be done
That he will do with me today ?

content.sanskrit:
अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथा परे ।
सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः
content.text:
Look forward, how [fared] the former ones.
Look backward ; so [will] the after ones.
Like grain a mortal ripens !
Like grain he is born hither (a-jayate) again!

content.sanskrit:
वैश्वानरः प्रविशति अतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान् ।
तस्यैता शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम्
content.text:
[Voice :]
As fire, enters
A Brahman ( brahmana ) guest into houses.
They make this the quieting thereof: —
Fetch water, Vaivasvata !

content.sanskrit:
आशाप्रतीक्षे सङ्गत सूनृतां च इष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूश्च सर्वान् ।
एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो यस्यानश्नन्वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे
content.text:
Hope and expectation, intercourse and pleasantness,
Sacrifices and meritorious deeds, sons and cattle, all —
This he snatches away from the man of little understanding
In whose home a Brahman remains without eating.
Three boons offered to Naciketas
[Death (Yama), returning from a three days’ absence and
finding that Naciketas has not received the hospitality which
is due to a Brahman, says:]

content.sanskrit:
तिस्रो रात्रीर्यदवात्सीर्गृहे मे अनश्नन् ब्रह्मन्नतिथिर्नमस्यः ।
नमस्तेऽस्तु ब्रह्मन्स्वस्ति मेऽस्तु तस्मात्प्रति त्रीन्वरान्वृणीष्व
content.text:
Since for three nights thou hast abode in my house
Without eating, O Brahman ( brahman ), a guest to be reverenced,
Reverence be to thee, O Brahman ! Well-being ( svasti ) be
Therefore in return choose three boons !
Naciketas’s first wish : return to an appeased father on earth
[Naciketas :]

content.sanskrit:
शान्तसङ्कल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माभिमृत्यो ।
त्वत्प्रसृष्टं माऽभिवदेत्प्रतीत एतत् त्रयाणां प्रथम वरं वृणे
content.text:
With intent appeased, well-minded, with passion departed,
That Gautama toward me may be, O Death ;
That cheerfully he may greet me, when from thee dismissed —
This of the three as boon the first I choose !

content.sanskrit:
यथा पुरस्ताद्भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः ।
सुख रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युः त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुक्तम्
content.text:
[Death :]
Cheerful as formerly will he be —
Auddalaki Aruni, from me dismissed.
Happily will he sleep o’ nights, with passion departed,
When he has seen thee from the mouth of Death released.

content.sanskrit:
स्वर्गे लोके न भयं किञ्चनास्ति न तत्र त्वं न जरया बिभेति ।
उभे तीर्त्वा अशनायापिपासे शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके
content.text:
[Naciketas:]
.In the heavenly world is no fear whatsoever.
Not there art thou. Not from old age does one fear.
Over both having crossed — hunger, and thirst too —
Gone beyond sorrow, one rejoices in the heaven-world.

content.sanskrit:
स त्वमग्नि स्वर्ग्यमध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि त्व श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम् ।
स्वर्गलोका अमृतत्वं भजन्त एतद् द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण
content.text:
Thyself, O Death, understandest the heavenly fire.
Declare it to me who have faith (sraddadhana).
Heaven-world people partake of immortality.
This I choose with boon the second.

content.sanskrit:
प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन् ।
अनन्तलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्धि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायाम्
content.text:
[Death :]
To thee I do declare, and do thou learn it of me —
Understanding about the heavenly fire, O Naciketas !
The attainment of the infinite world, likewise too its establishment—
Know thou that as set down in the secret place [of the heart].

content.sanskrit:
लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्मै या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा ।
स चापि तत्प्रत्यवदद्यथोक्तं अथास्य मृत्युः पुनरेवाह तुष्टः
content.text:
[Narrative :]
He told him of that fire as the beginning of the world,
What bricks, and how many, and how [built].
And he too repeated that, as it was told.
Then, pleased with him, Death said again —

content.sanskrit:
तमब्रवीत्प्रीयमाणो महात्मा वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः ।
तवैव नाम्ना भवितायमग्निः सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण
content.text:
Delighting, the great soul ( mahatman ) said to him: —
[Death resumes :]
A further boon I give thee here today.
By thy name indeed shall this fire be [known].
This multifold garland ( srnka ), too, accept.

content.sanskrit:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू ।
ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा निचाय्य मा शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति
content.text:
Having kindled a triple Naciketas-fire, having attained union
with the three,
Performing the triple work, one crosses over birth and death.
By knowing the knower of what is born from Brahma, the
god to be praised,
[And] by revering [him], one goes for ever to this [peace
( santi ).

content.sanskrit:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा य एवं विद्वाश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् ।
स मृत्युपाशान्पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके
content.text:
Having kindled a triple Naciketas-fire, having known this triad,
He who knowing thus, builds up the Naciketas-fire —
He, having cast off in advance the bonds of death,
With sorrow overpassed, rejoices in the heaven-world.

content.sanskrit:
एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण ।
एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासः तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व
content.text:
This, O Naciketas, is thy heavenly fire,
Which thou didst choose with the second boon.
As thine, indeed, will folks proclaim this fire,
The third boon, Naciketas, choose !

content.sanskrit:
येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये अस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके ।
एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाऽहं वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः
content.text:
[Naciketas :]
This doubt that there is in regard to a man deceased :
* He exists,’ say some ; ‘ He exists not,’ say others —
This would I know, instructed by thee !
Of the boons this is boon the third.

content.sanskrit:
देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा न हि सुविज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः ।
अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम्
content.text:
[Death :]
Even the gods had doubt as to this of yore !
For truly, it is not easily to be understood. Subtile is this
matter ( dharma ).
Another boon, O Naciketas, choose !
Press me not ! Give up this one for me !

content.sanskrit:
देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ ।
वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित्
content.text:
[Naciketas :]
Even the gods had doubt, indeed, as to this,
And thou, O Death, sayest that it is not easily to be understood.
And another declarer of it the like of thee is not to be obtained.
No other boon the equal of it is there at all.

content.sanskrit:
शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान्वृणीष्वा बहून्पशून् हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान् ।
भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि
content.text:
[Death :]
Choose centenarian sons and grandsons,
Many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses.
Choose a great abode of earth.
And thyself live as many autumns as thou desirest.

content.sanskrit:
एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च ।
महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि
content.text:
This, if thou thinkest an equal boon,
Choose — wealth and long life !
A great one on earth, O Naciketas, be thou.
The enjoyer of thy desires I make thee.

content.sanskrit:
ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके सर्वान् कामाश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व ।
इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः ।
आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतो मरणं माऽनुप्राक्षीः
content.text:
Whate’er desires are hard to get in mortal world —
For all desires at pleasure make request.
These lovely maidens with chariots, with lyres —
Such [maidens], indeed, are not obtainable by men —
By these, from me bestowed, be waited on
O Naciketas, question me not regarding dying ( marana )

content.sanskrit:
श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत् सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः ।
अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते
content.text:
[Naciketas :]
Ephemeral things! That which is a mortal’s, O End-maker,
Even the vigor (tejas ) of all the powers, they wear away.
Even a whole life is slight indeed.
Thine be the vehicles (vaha) ! Thine be the dance and song!

content.sanskrit:
न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा ।
जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव
content.text:
Not with wealth is a man to be satisfied.
Shall we take wealth, if we have seen thee ?
Shall we live so long as thou shalt rule?
— This, in truth, is the boon to be chosen by me.

content.sanskrit:
अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य जीर्यन्मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् ।
अभिध्यायन्वर्णरतिप्रमोदान् अतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत
content.text:
When one has come into the presence of undecaying immortals,
What decaying mortal here below that understands,
That meditates upon the pleasures of beauty and delight,
Would delight in a life over-long?

content.sanskrit:
यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् ।
योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते
content.text:
This thing whereon they doubt, O Death:
What there is in the great passing-on — tell us that
This boon, that has entered into the hidden —
No other than that does Naciketas choose.

content.sanskrit: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषं सिनीतः । तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥
content.transliteration: anyachchreyo'nyadutaiva preyaste ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṁ sinītaḥ | tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate'rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ||
content.text:
The better ( sreyas ) is one thing, and the pleasanter ( preyas )
quite another.
Both these, of different aim, bind a person.
Of these two, well is it for him who takes the better;
He fails of his aim who chooses the pleasanter.

content.sanskrit:
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः
तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः ।
श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते
प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते
content.text:
Both the better and the pleasanter come to a man.
Going all around the two, the wise man discriminates.
The wise man chooses the better, indeed, rather than the
pleasanter.
The stupid man, from getting-and-keeping ( yoga-ksema ), chooses
the pleasanter.

content.sanskrit:
स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामान्
अभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ।
नैता सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो
यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः
content.text:
Thou indeed, upon the pleasant and pleasantly appearing
desires
Meditating, hast let them go, O Naciketas.
Thou art not one who has taken that garland of wealth
In which many men sink down.

content.sanskrit:
दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची
अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता ।
विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये
न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त
content.text:
Widely opposite and asunder are these two :
Ignorance ( avidya ) and what is known as ‘ knowledge ’ ( vidya ).
I think Naciketas desirous of obtaining knowledge!
Many desires rend thee not.

content.sanskrit:
अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः
स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः ।
दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा
अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः
content.text:
Those abiding in the midst of ignorance,
Self-wise, thinking themselves learned,
Running hither and thither, go around deluded,
Like blind men led by one who is himself blind.

content.sanskrit:
न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं
प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् ।
अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी
पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे
content.text:
The passing-on is not clear to him who is childish,
Heedless, deluded with the delusion of wealth.
Thinking ‘ This is the world ! There is no other ! ’ —
Again and again he comes under my control.

content.sanskrit:
श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः
शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः ।
आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धा
आश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः
content.text:
He who by many is not obtainable even to hear of,
He whom many, even when hearing, know not —
Wonderful is the declarer, proficient the obtainer of Him!
Wonderful the knower, proficiently taught !

content.sanskrit:
न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त
एष सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः ।
अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्ति
अणीयान्ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात्
content.text:
Not, when proclaimed by an inferior man, is He
To be well understood, [though] being manifoldly considered.
Unless declared by another, there is no going thither;
For He is inconceivably more subtile than what is of subtile
measure.

content.sanskrit:
नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया
प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ ।
यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि
त्वादृङ् नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा
content.text:
Not by reasoning ( tarka ) is this thought ( mati ) to be attained.
Proclaimed by another, indeed, it is for easy understanding,
dearest friend ( prestha)\ —
This which thou hast attained ! Ah, thou art of true steadfastness !
May there be for us a questioner (prasta) the like of thee,
O Naciketas!
Steadfast renunciation and self-meditation required
[Naciketas :]

content.sanskrit:
जानाम्यह शेवधिरित्यनित्यं
न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत् ।
ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निरनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम्
content.text:
I know that what is known as treasure is something inconstant.
For truly, that which is steadfast is not obtained by those
who are unsteadfast.
Therefore the Naciketas-fire has been built up by me,
And with means which are inconstant I have obtained that
which is constant.

content.sanskrit:
कामस्याप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां
क्रतोरानन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् ।
स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां
दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः
content.text:
[Death :]
The obtainment of desire, the foundation of the world ( jagat ),
The endlessness of will, the safe shore of fearlessness,
The greatness of praise, the wide extent, the foundation
(having seen *),
Thou, O Naciketas, a wise one, hast with steadfastness let
[these] go !

content.sanskrit:
तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं
गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम् ।
अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं
मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति
content.text:
Him who is hard to see, entered into the hidden,
Set in the secret place [of the heart], dwelling in the depth,
primeval —
By considering him as God, through the Yoga-study of what
pertains to self,
The wise man leaves joy and sorrow behind.

content.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः
प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य ।
स मोदते मोदनीयं हि लब्ध्वा
विवृत सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये
content.text:
Y hen a mortal has heard this and fully comprehended,
Has torn off what is concerned with the right ( dharmya ), and
has taken Him as the subtile,
Then he rejoices, for indeed he has obtained what is to be
rejoiced in.
I regard Naciketas a dwelling open [for Atman].

content.sanskrit:
अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मादन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात् ।
अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च
यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद
content.text:
Apart from the right ( dharma ) and apart from the unright
( a-dharma ),
Apart from both what has been done and what has not been
done here,
Apart from what has been and what is to be —
What thou seest as that, speak that !
[Naciketas being unable to mention that absolutely unqualified object, Death continues to explain :]

content.sanskrit:
सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति
तपांसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति ।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण ब्रवीम्योमित्येतत्
content.text:
The word which all the Vedas rehearse,
And which all austerities proclaim,
Desiring which men live the life of religious studentship
( brahmacarya ) —
That word to thee I briefly declare.
That is Om !

content.sanskrit:
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् ।
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत्
content.text:
That syllable, truly, indeed, is Brahma !
That syllable indeed is the supreme !
Knowing that syllable, truly, indeed,
Whatever one desires is his !

content.sanskrit:
एतदालम्बनँ श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम् ।
एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
content.text:
That is the best support.
That is the supreme support.
Knowing that support,
One becomes happy in the Brahma-world.

content.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे
content.text:
The wise one [i. e. the soul, the atman, the self] is not born,
nor dies.
This one has not come from anywhere, has not become anyone.
Unborn, constant, eternal, primeval, this one
Is not slain when the body is slain.

content.sanskrit:
हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुँ हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायँ हन्ति न हन्यते
content.text:
If the slayer think to slay.
If the slain think himself slain,
Both these understand not.
This one slays not, nor is slain.

content.sanskrit:
अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्माऽस्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम् ।
तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको
धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः
content.text:
More minute than the minute, greater than the great
Is the Soul (Atman) that is set in the heart of a creature here.
One who is without the active will ( a-kratu ) beholds Him,
and becomes freed from sorrow —
When through the grace ( prasada ) of the Creator ( dhatr ) he
beholds the greatness of the Soul (Atman).

content.sanskrit:
आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः ।
कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति
content.text:
Sitting, he proceeds afar;
Lying, he goes everywhere.
Who else than I (mad) is able to know
The god ( deva ) who rejoices and rejoices not ( madamada )?

content.sanskrit:
अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
content.text:
Him who is the bodiless among bodies,
Stable among the unstable,
The great, all-pervading Soul (Atman) —
On recognizing Him, the wise man sorrows not.

content.sanskrit:
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो
न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।
यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्य
स्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनू स्वाम्
content.text:
This Soul (Atman) is not to be obtained by instruction,
Nor by intellect, nor by much learning.
He is to be obtained only by the one whom He chooses ;
To such a one that Soul (Atman) reveals his own person
( tanum svam ).

content.sanskrit:
नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः ।
नाशान्तमानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात्
content.text:
Not he who has not ceased from bad conduct,
Not he who is not tranquil, not he who is not composed,
Not he who is not of peaceful mind
Can obtain Him by intelligence ( prajna ).

content.sanskrit:
यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः ।
मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः
content.text:
He for whom the priesthood ( brahman ) and the nobility
( ksatra )
Both are as food,
And death is as a sauce —
Who really knows where He is?

content.sanskrit:
ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे ।
छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः
content.text:
There are two that drink of righteousness ( rta ) in the world
of good deeds ;
Both are entered into the secret place [of the heart], and in
the highest upper sphere.
Brahma-knowers speak of them as ‘ light ’ and ‘ shade,’
And so do householders who maintain the five sacrificial fires,
and those too who perform the triple Naciketas-fire.

content.sanskrit:
यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्परम् ।
अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं नाचिकेतं शकेमहि
content.text:
This which is the bridge for those who sacrifice,
And which is the highest imperishable Brahma
For those who seek to cross over to the fearless farther
shore —
The Naciketas-fire may we master !

content.sanskrit:
आत्मानं रथितं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु ।
बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च
content.text:
Know thou the soul ( atman , self) as riding in a chariot.
The body as the chariot.
Know thou the intellect ( buddhi ) as the chariot-driver,
And the mind ( manas ) as the reins.

content.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयां स्तेषु गोचरान् ।
आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः
content.text:
The senses ( indriya ), they say, are the horses ;
The objects of sense, what they range over.
The self combined with senses and mind
Wise men call ‘ the enjoyer ’ ( bhoktr ).

content.sanskrit:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः
content.text:
He who has not understanding ( a-vijnana ),
Whose mind is not constantly held firm —
His senses are uncontrolled,
Like the vicious horses of a chariot-driver.

content.sanskrit:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः
content.text:
He, however, who has understanding,
Whose mind is constantly held firm —
His senses are under control,
Like the good horses of a chariot-driver.

content.sanskrit:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः ।
न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति
content.text:
He, however, who has not understanding,
Who is unmindful and ever impure,
Reaches not the goal.
But goes on to transmigration ( samsara ).

content.sanskrit:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः ।
स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते
content.text:
He, however, who has understanding,
Who is mindful and ever pure,
Reaches the goal
From which he is born no more.

content.sanskrit:
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनः प्रग्रहवान्नरः ।
सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम्
content.text:
He, however, who has the understanding of a chariot- driver,
A man who reins in his mind —
He reaches the end of his journey,
That highest place of Vishnu.

content.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः
content.text:
Higher than the senses are the objects of sense.
Higher than the objects of sense is the mind ( manas ) ;
And higher than the mind is the intellect ( buddhi ).
Higher than the intellect is the Great Self (Atman).

content.sanskrit:
महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः ।
पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः
content.text:
Higher than the Great is the Unmanifest ( avyakta ).
Higher than the Unmanifest is the Person.
Higher than the Person there is nothing at all.
That is the goal. That is the highest course.

content.sanskrit:
एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽत्मा न प्रकाशते ।
दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः
content.text:
Though He is hidden in all things,
That Soul (Atman, Self) shines not forth.
But he is seen by subtle seers
With superior, subtle intellect.

content.sanskrit:
यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि ।
ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि
content.text:
An intelligent man should suppress his speech and his mind.
The latter he should suppress in the Understanding-Self
(jnana atman).
The understanding he should suppress in the Great Self
[= buddhi, intellect].
That he should suppress in the Tranquil Self ( santa atman).

content.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥
content.transliteration: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varānnibodhata | kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṁ pathastatkavayo vadanti ||
content.text:
Arise ye ! Awake ye !
Obtain your boons and understand them !
A sharpened edge of a razor, hard to traverse,
A difficult path is this — poets ( kavi ) declare !

content.sanskrit:
अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथाऽरसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् ।
अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तं मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते
content.text:
What is soundless, touchless, formless, imperishable,
Likewise tasteless, constant, odorless,
Without beginning, without end, higher than the great, stable —
By discerning That, one is liberated from the mouth of death.

content.sanskrit:
नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तँ सनातनम् ।
उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
content.text:
The Naciketas tale,
Death’s immemorial teaching —
By declaring and hearing this, a wise man
Is magnified in the Brahma-world.

content.sanskrit:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद् ब्रह्मसंसदि ।
प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते । तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति
content.text:
If one recites this supreme secret
In an assembly of Brahmans,
Or at a time of the ceremony for the dead, devoutly —
That makes for immortality !
— That makes for immortality!

content.sanskrit:
पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् ।
कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन्
content.text:
The Self-existent ( svayambhu ) pierced the openings [of the
senses] outward ;
Therefore one looks outward, not within himself ( antaratman ).
A certain wise man, while seeking immortality,
Introspectively beheld the Soul (Atman) face to face.

content.sanskrit:
पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् ।
अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा
ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते
content.text:
The childish go after outward pleasures ;
They walk into the net of widespread death.
But the wise, knowing immortality,
Seek not the stable among things which are unstable here.

content.sanskrit:
येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शांश्च मैथुनान् ।
एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
That by which [one discerns] form, taste, smell,
Sound, and mutual touches —
It is with That indeed that one discerns.
What is there left over here !
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
content.text:
By recognizing as the great pervading Soul (Atman)
That whereby one perceives both
The sleeping state and the waking state,
The wise man sorrows not.

content.sanskrit:
य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् ।
ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
He who knows this experiencer
As the living Soul (Atman) near at hand,
Lord of what has been and of what is to be —
He does not shrink away from Him.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
He who was born of old from austerity (/ apas ),
Was born of old from the waters,
Who stands entered into the secret place [of the heart].
Who looked forth through beings —
This,' verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
या प्राणेन सम्भवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
She who arises with life (prana),
Aditi (Infinity), maker of divinity,
Who stands entered into the secret place [of the heart],
Who was born forth through beings —
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
अरण्योर्निर्हितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः ।
दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
Fire (Agni), the all-knower (Jatavedas ), hidden away in the
two fire-sticks
Like the embryo well borne by pregnant women,
Worthy to be worshiped day by day
By watchful men with oblations —
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
यतश्चोदेति सूर्यः अस्तं यत्र च गच्छति ।
तं देवाः सर्वे अर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
Whence the sun rises,
And where it goes to rest —
On Him all the gods are founded ;
And no one ever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति
content.text:
Whatever is here, that is there.
What is there, that again is here.
He obtains death after death
Who seems to see a difference here.

content.sanskrit:
मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति
content.text:
By the mind, indeed, is this [realization] to be attained : —
There is no difference here at all !
He goes from death to death
Who seems to see a difference here.

content.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति ।
ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb
Stands in the midst of one’s self ( atman ),
Lord of what has been and of what is to be.
One does not shrink away from Him.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः ।
ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb,
Like a light without smoke,
Lord of what has been and what is to be.
He alone is today, and tomorrow too.

content.sanskrit:
यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति ।
एवं धर्मान् पृथक्पश्यंस्तानेवानुविधावति
content.text:
As water rained upon rough ground
Runs to waste among the hills,
So he who sees qualities ( dharma ) separately,
Runs to waste after them.

content.sanskrit:
यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति ।
एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम
content.text:
As pure water poured forth into pure
Becomes the very same,
So becomes the soul ( atman ), O Gautama,
Of the seer (muni) who has understanding.

content.sanskrit:
पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः ।
अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
By ruling over the eleven-gated citadel
Of the Unborn, the Un-crooked-minded one,
One sorrows not.
But when liberated [from the body], he is liberated indeed.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
हसः शुचिषद्वसुरान्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।
नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत्
content.text:
The swan [i. e. sun] in the clear, the Vasu in the atmosphere,
The priest by the altar, the guest in the house,
In man, in broad space, in the right ( rta ), in the sky,
Born in water, born in cattle, born in the right, born in rock,
is the Right, the Great !

content.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयति अपानं प्रत्यगस्यति ।
मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते
content.text:
Upwards the out-breath ( prana ) he leadeth.
The in-breath ( apana ) inwards he casts.
The dwarf who is seated in the middle
All the gods ( deva ) reverence !

content.sanskrit:
अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः ।
देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
When this incorporate one that stands in the body
Is dissolved,
And is released from the body,
What is there left over here ?
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन ।
इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ
content.text:
Not by the out-breath (prana) and the in-breath ( apana )
Doth any mortal whatsoever live.
But by another do men live —
Even That whereon both these depend.

content.sanskrit:
हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम
content.text:
Come ! I will declare this to you :
The hidden, eternal Brahma;
And how, after it reaches death,
The soul (atman) fares, O Gautama !

content.sanskrit:
योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः ।
स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम्
content.text:
Some go into a womb
For the embodiment of a corporeal being.
Others go into a stationary thing
According to their deeds ( karman ), according to their
knowledge.

content.sanskrit:
य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
He who is awake in those that sleep,
The Person who fashions desire after desire —
That indeed is the Pure. That is Brahma.
That indeed is called the Immortal.
On it all the worlds do rest ;
And no one soever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च
content.text:
As the one fire has entered the world
And becomes corresponding in form to every form,
So the one Inner Soul (Atman) of all things
Is corresponding in form to every form, and yet is outside.

content.sanskrit:
वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च
content.text:
As the one wind has entered the world
And becomes corresponding in form to every form,
So the one Inner Soul of all things
Is corresponding in form to every form, and yet is outside.

content.sanskrit:
सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः
content.text:
As the sun, the eye of the whole world,
Is not sullied by the external faults of the eyes,
So the one Inner Soul of all things
Is not sullied by the evil in the world, being external to it.

content.sanskrit:
एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम्
content.text:
The Inner Soul ( antaratman ) of all things, the One Controller,
Who makes his one form manifold —
The wise who perceive Him as standing in oneself,
They, and no others, have eternal happiness !

content.sanskrit:
नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरा
स्तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम्
content.text:
Him who is the constant among the inconstant, the intelligent
among intelligences,
The One among many, who grants desires —
The wise who perceive Him as standing in oneself,
They, and no others, have eternal peace !

content.sanskrit:
तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् ।
कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा
content.text:
‘This is it!’ — thus they recognize
The highest, indescribable happiness.
How, now, shall I understand ‘ this ’ ?
Does it shine [of itself] or does it shine in reflection?

content.sanskrit:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं
नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं
तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति
content.text:
The sun shines not there, nor the moon and stars,
These lightnings shine not, much less this (earthly) fire !
After Him, as He shines, doth everything shine,
This whole world is illumined with His light.

content.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शातख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
content.text:
Its root is above, its branches below —
This eternal fig-tree !
That (root) indeed is the Pure. That is Brahma.
That indeed is called the Immortal.
On it all the worlds do rest,
And no one soever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

content.sanskrit:
यदिदं किंच जगत्सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् ।
महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति
content.text:
This whole world, whatever there is,
Was created from and moves in Life (prana).
The great fear, the upraised thunderbolt —
They who know That, become immortal.

content.sanskrit:
भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः ।
भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः
content.text:
From fear of Him fire (Agni) doth burn.
From fear the sun (Surya) gives forth heat.
From fear both Indra and Wind (Vayu),
And Death (Mrityu) as fifth, do speed along.
Degrees of perception of the Soul (Atman).

content.sanskrit:
इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्शरीरस्य विस्रसः ।
ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते
content.text:
If one has been able to perceive [Him] here on earth
Before the dissolution of the body,
According to that [knowledge] he becomes fitted
For embodiment in the world-creations.

content.sanskrit:
यथादर्शे तथाऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके ।
यथाऽप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके
च्छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके

इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् ।
पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
content.text:
The separate nature of the senses,
And that their arising and setting
Is of things that come into being apart [from himself],
The wise man recognizes, and sorrows not.

content.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम्

अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च ।
यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति
content.text:
Higher than the Unmanifest, however, is the Person
(Purusha),
All-pervading and without any mark ( a-linga ) whatever.
Knowing which, a man is liberated
And goes to immortality.

content.sanskrit:
न सन्दृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य
न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् ।
हृदा मनीषा मनसाऽभिक्लृप्तो
य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति
content.text:
His form is not to be beheld.
No one soever sees Him with the eye.
He is framed by the heart, by the thought, by the mind.
They who know That become immortal.

content.sanskrit:
यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह ।
बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टति तामाहुः परमां गतिम्
content.text:
When cease the five
[Sense-]knowledges, together with the mind ( manas ),
And the intellect ( buddhi ) stirs not —
That, they say, is the highest course.

content.sanskrit:
तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् ।
अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ
content.text:
This they consider as Yoga —
The firm holding back of the senses.
Then one becomes undistracted.
Yoga, truly, is the origin and the end.

content.sanskrit:
नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा ।
अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते
content.text:
Not by speech, not by mind,
Not by sight can He be apprehended.
How can He be comprehended
Otherwise than by one’s saying ‘ He is ’ ?

content.sanskrit:
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः ।
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति
content.text:
He can indeed be comprehended by the thought ‘He is’
(asti)
And by [admitting] the real nature of both [his comprehensibility and his incomprehensibility].
When he has been comprehended by the thought ‘He is’
His real nature manifests itself.

content.sanskrit:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते
content.text:
When are liberated all
The desires that lodge in one’s heart,
Then a mortal becomes immortal !
Therein he reaches Brahma !

content.sanskrit:
यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम्
content.text:
When are cut all
The knots of the heart here on earth,
Then a mortal becomes immortal !
— Thus far is the instruction.

content.sanskrit:
शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका ।
तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति
विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति
content.text:
There are a hundred and one arteries of the heart.
One of these passes up to the crown of the head.
Going up by it, one goes to immortality.
The others are for departing in various directions.

content.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा
सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः ।
तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण ।
तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति
content.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb is the inner soul
( antaratman ),
Ever seated in the heart of creatures.
Him one should draw out from one’s own body
Like an arrow-shaft out from a reed, with firmness.
Him one should know as the Pure, the Immortal —
Yea, Him one should know as the Pure, the Immortal.

content.sanskrit:
मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् ।
ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्युरन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव
content.text:
Then Naciketas, having received this knowledge
Declared by Death, and the entire rule of Yoga,
Attained Brahma and became free from passion, free from death ;
And so may any other who knows this in regard to the Soul
(Atman).
